오늘의 매수/매도 시그널

DBC 구성 비중이 큰 에너지·곡물·금속 전반에 걸친 공급 제약이 동시에 터지고 있다. - **로이터(El Niño) & 시킹알파(유가/설탕)**: 2026~27년 슈퍼 엘니뇨로 코코아·커피·설탕 등 소프트 커모디티 공급 충격 예고, 미-이란 긴장에 따른 유가 리스크 프리미엄 지속, 설탕 2025년 5월 이후 최고치 경신 등 **섹터별 추가 상승 재료**가 산재해 있다. 3. **일목균형표(보조 참고) 상충에 따른 리스크 관리:** 현재 주가는 구름 **위**에 있으나 구름 자체가 **음운(하락 구름)**이다. 기계적 규칙(돌파 매수)과 보조 지표(중장기 구름 음전)가 엇갈린다. 이는 추세 전환 초기이거나, 상승 추세가 아직 견고하지 않음을 시사한다. **진입 시 기본 비중의 50~60%만 우선 투입(half-size entry)**하고, 주가가 구름 상단을 확실히 이탈해 양운으로 전환되거나 100일 상단도 돌파할 때 나머지 비중을 채우는 **피라미딩/분할 진입**으로 리스크를 관리하라. 손절 라인은 기계적 트레일링 스탑(29.78)을 철저히 준수한다.

Explainer-Why a super El Niño leaves tropical commodities acutely exposed | 95.5 WIFC
Thomson Reuters · 2026-08-18T00:00:00.000Z

Summary tailored to your query: commodities market outlook analysis - El Niño is strengthening and could become a very strong event in 2026-27, raising global temperatures, altering rainfall, and adding risk for crops worldwide. - Soft commodities (tropical crops) are particularly exposed due to El Niño-driven droughts, heat, and irregular rainfall patterns. - Cocoa: Half of world production in Ivory Coast and Ghana; prior El Niño years have reduced cocoa output. Prices spiked in 2024 on West African harvest failures. - Coffee (robusta and arabica): - Robusta: Vietnam and Indonesia (top producers) often suffer drought and heat during El Niño, reducing yields from mid-year onward. - Arabica: Brazil benefits temporarily from potential frost protection during harvests, but long-term dryness and heat later in the season can depress output for the next crop (potentially 2027). - Sugar: Typically sees excess rains in Brazil during El Niño, potentially hurting harvest quality, while India and Thailand may experience reduced rainfall during monsoon; India could see notably lower rainfall in the 2026 monsoon, risking about 1 million metric tons of output loss. - Overall sentiment: Past El Niño episodes have correlated with stronger price moves in soft commodities; however, long-term dynamics in sugar and coffee are nuanced, with some regions potentially benefiting in certain windows. - Near-term drivers: El Niño’s development, rainfall and temperature anomalies, and macro costs (fertilizers, energy) tied to broader geopolitical tensions can compound price volatility. - Outlook takeaway: Expect higher volatility and potential price firings in cocoa, coffee, and sugar through late 2026 into 2027, driven by regional weather shocks in key producing areas; Brazil remains a pivotal factor for sugar and coffee supply, with possible timing-dependent effects on prices.
